Regressions7 — new problems introduced by the fixes

These are the cost of the round. Each was found by a tester and then confirmed by me in the source. They are worth fixing before the next batch, because three of them undo part of the fix that introduced them.
regressionmajor The panel-model fixes are scoped to ≤900px — 901–1599px gets none of them7 testers
Evidence
08-atlas.png: the Atlas popover opens with filter chips 'All / ★ 0 / ⚑ / ❄' and a Travel Home button — no heading anywhere. 09-compendium.png: opens straight into '📖 Species / 🗂 Binder' tabs — no heading. 12-charters.png: opens on '⚑ CHAPTER 1 — OFF THE ROCK', which is content, not a panel name. Source: the ::before titles that give these panels their names (#log::before 'Star Atlas', #codex::before 'Compendium', #chpanel::before 'Charters', index.html:1726-1732) sit inside @media (max-width:900px), which opens at :1675 and closes at :1735. My viewport is 1920px. None of the three carries role="dialog" or aria-label either — only 5 of the ~14 surfaces do (index.html:1929, 1985, 2014, 2113, 2141), and these three are not among them.
Impact
Three of the game's five main boards announce themselves as an unnamed group of controls. Even the CSS comment at :1725 says 'the sheet announces WHAT it is — no more untitled bands' — that promise was kept on phones and skipped on desktop. I open a panel and have to infer from its contents which one I am in.
Suggested fix
Move the ::before title rules out of the max-width:900px block so all widths get them, and add role="dialog" aria-label to #log, #codex, #chpanel, #yardcard, #records and #tray so the name reaches assistive tech and not just the eye.
Reported by
accessibility/desktop-1080, button-masher/pixel-7, cautious-newbie/surface-pro, explorer/ultrawide, min-maxer/ipad-pro-13, speedrunner/ipad-land, speedrunner/ipad-land, stress-tester/laptop-720, accessibility/desktop-1080
regressionmajor Records and Notifications now print their title twice (new)6 testers

pixel-7__11-records.png shows '🏆 RECORDS' at y~287 and then '🏆 Records' again at y~337. pixel-7__16-notifications.png shows '🔔 NOTIFICATIONS' at y~280 and 'NOTIFICATIONS' again at y~361. Source: the new mobile sheet title #records::before / #tray::before (index.html:1730-1731) was added on top of headers these two panels already render themselves — renderRecords() emits '<div class="chead">🏆 Records</div>' (index.html:23898) and the tray markup has '<div class="thead"><span>Notifications</span>' (index.html:1909). Star Atlas, Compendium and Charters have no inner header and show one title each, correctly.

Two panels out of nine say their own name twice on first open. It reads as a half-applied patch and it burns ~50px of a 915px screen, pushing the last row of every list under the panel's clipped edge.
Suggested fix
Drop the ::before for #records and #tray only (keep it for #log, #codex, #chpanel), or delete the inner .chead / .thead label and let the sheet title carry it.

regressionmajor Toasts render behind the Field Training card (new)2 testers
Evidence
iphone-se__02-after-name.png: a ghost of a toast is visible THROUGH the Field Training card — uppercase '…ITION SAVED' sits behind the 'FIELD TRAINING' label, and '…s automatically… this device' / 'no account needed.' sits behind the body copy. Source confirms: index.html:15733 fires toast('✓ Expedition saved', 'Progress saves automatically on this device — no account needed.') on the first save; #toast is z-index:40 (index.html:813) and on ≤900px docks to top:calc(var(--topbar-h,110px) + 8px) (index.html:1842); #tutbox is z-index:50 at top:calc(var(--topbar-h,96px) + 6px) (index.html:1185-1186). Same lane, 2px apart, the toast loses. By 03 the toast has expired unseen.
Impact
The source comment at index.html:15729 says this toast was added in v1.7.2 specifically for the cautious-newbie persona, because the only save messaging used to be a data-loss warning above the red Reset button. It is the single most reassuring sentence in the game for a first-timer worried about losing progress — and on the smallest iPhone it is delivered underneath an opaque card and never read. The new top toast lane broke the fix that was written for me.
Suggested fix
Raise #toast above #tutbox (z-index 60), or offset the toast lane by the training card's height while body.training is pending. Better: since toast() already suppresses pop-ups during training (index.html:15149), also suppress in the window between name submit and the training card mounting — queue '✓ Expedition saved' and flush it when training ends, or render it as a line inside the Field Training card itself.
Reported by

regressionmajor Stale survey card leaks out from behind every centred tablet sheet1 tester
Evidence
ipad-mini__08-atlas, 09-compendium, 11-records, 12-charters, 14-settings, 16-notifications — six of sixteen frames. In every one the Mercury survey card is still open behind the sheet, and because the new 701-900px band centres sheets at 600px on a 744px screen, the card's right edge shows through the ~72px gutter: its ✕ at the top right, then 'impact', 'EXPAND', 'MINERAL VEINS / Aluminium · Iron · Calcium · Chromium · 1,507 pulls left' and a cut-off 'GROUND SURVEYED' tag stacked down the right side. Source confirms it: the PANELS registry that closePanels() walks (index.html:23776-23799) contains log, codex, charters, events, sheet, yard, records, tray, set, guide, prime — #panel is not a member, so opening a board never closes the survey card. At <=700px the sheets are left:8px/right:8px (index.html:1725-1731) and fully cover the 300px card, so this is specific to the new tablet band.
Impact
Every board I open looks half-broken, and there are two ✕ glyphs on screen ~120px apart (e.g. sheet ✕ at the Atlas title row and card ✕ just above-right of it). I tap one expecting to get back to the map and land somewhere I didn't ask for. That is exactly the hard backtracking I hate.
Suggested fix
Add the survey card to the PANELS registry as a closeable surface (or call the card's own close from closePanels when `except` is truthy, next to the existing toast flush at index.html:23803-23808). Failing that, in the 701-900px block make the sheet's scrim opaque enough to bury anything under it, or widen sheets to `calc(100vw - 16px)` on portrait tablets so no gutter exists.

What's still open76 issue clusters this round

2 critical, 37 major, 28 minor, 9 polish. Ranked by severity then how many independent testers hit them.

critical No focus management: dialogs declare aria-modal but do not trap or restore focusaccessibility 1 tester · 1 device
Evidence
13-prime-codex.png shows the Prime Codex as a real modal with a blurred, dimmed backdrop over the whole page. Source: #pcdxbtn is at index.html:1901, #primebox at :2113. There are only five .focus() calls in 24,308 lines (index.html:5310, 16180, 22348, 22360, 22370) and all five target text inputs — nothing focuses a dialog on open. So after activating the Prime Codex chip with Enter, focus stays on the chip and Tab must walk the eight visible controls that sit between them in the DOM — #searchin, #bell, #setbtn, #chbtn, #logbtn, #codexbtn, #cargobtn, #recbtn — all eight of which are behind the backdrop and visually unavailable. The ninth Tab finally enters the dialog. Closing is worse: the panel is display:none'd with the focus still inside it, focus falls to <body>, and the next Tab restarts at the top of the document. refocus() (index.html:5301) only fires on in-place re-renders, never on close, and there is no lastFocus save/restore anywhere in the file.
Impact
Every board in the game costs a blind walk through invisible furniture to enter and loses my place entirely on exit. Opening the Records board, reading one line and closing it means re-tabbing from the top bar. Across a session this is the single biggest tax on a keyboard user, and it is what makes the otherwise-good panel content feel unreachable.
Suggested fix
On open, store document.activeElement and call .focus() on the dialog's first interactive child (or the dialog itself with tabindex="-1"). On close, restore focus to the stored element. Wire it once into the PANELS registry open/close pair (index.html:23780-23800) and the Escape stack (index.html:5347) so all fourteen surfaces inherit it.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
Evidence
13-prime-codex.png and 15-guide.png both show true modals: full-viewport dimmed, blurred backdrops over the whole page. Source: grep for key==='Tab' returns nothing — there is no trap. grep for 'inert' returns no attribute use, and the only aria-hidden values in the file are on three decorative SVGs (index.html:1874, 2028, 2073) and the canvas (:2224). Nothing is applied to the page behind an open dialog.
Impact
The five surfaces that correctly declare aria-modal="true" lie to assistive tech: the property says the rest of the page is inert, and it isn't. Tabbing forward from the Guide's last row lands me on the survey card behind it; a screen reader will happily read the entire obscured page as live content. It is the worst of both worlds — the visual treatment says modal, the semantics say nothing is.
Suggested fix
On open, set inert on the page container behind the dialog (or aria-hidden="true" plus a Tab-cycling handler). Removing it on close is one line and fixes all five dialogs at once.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
critical Search results are click-only, closing the last non-canvas route to a worldaccessibility 1 tester · 1 device
Evidence
The 'Search discoveries or paste code' box is visible top-right in every storyboard state. Source index.html:16280 renders each result as <div class="sr" data-sri="i"> — no role, no tabindex, no aria. The only activation path is searchRes.addEventListener('click', ...) at :16295. The keydown handler at :16288 handles exactly two keys: Enter re-runs the search (or travels, but only if the text matches /cf1-/i), and Escape closes the list. There is no arrow-key navigation of the result list and no Enter-selects-first-result.
Impact
With the board itself dead, search was the one remaining way I could reach a world by name. I can type into it, I can see the match render, and I cannot get to it. The only thing that does work is pasting a cf1- share code someone else generated with a mouse — I cannot originate a single destination on my own.
Suggested fix
Give each .sr row role="option" and tabindex="0" inside a role="listbox", wire ArrowUp/ArrowDown from the input to move aria-activedescendant, and make Enter commit the highlighted row. This one change would give a keyboard user a real, if narrow, way into the game universe while the canvas work is pending.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
major The Cratered/Carbon world fix is cancelled by text-transform:uppercaseconsistency 6 testers · 7 devices
Evidence
Screenshot 11 shows both labels simultaneously: the survey card header reads 'Mercury / CRATERED WORLD' while the Records Expedition Journal overlapping it reads 'Mercury Carbon world · 7/26'. Screenshot 07's header reads 'PLANETFALL — MERCURY · CARBON WORLD'; screenshots 06, 08, 09, 12, 14, 16 all keep saying 'CRATERED WORLD'. The source shows this was a known v1.7.2 fix attempt — comment at line 12603: "'PLANETFALL — CARBON WORLD' vs the card's 'CRATERED WORLD' read as a contradiction — the header now leads with the world's NAME and the landing region follows lowercase, visibly subordinate" — and line 12609 does build the string with `.toLowerCase()`. But `#vistabox .vh{...text-transform:uppercase...}` at line 1651 uppercases the whole header again, so the subordination the fix depended on is invisible.
Impact
I read everything before I click; that is my whole approach. When two panels open at once disagree about what kind of world I am standing on, I can't tell whether I misread something, whether landing changed the world, or whether the game is broken — and I stop trusting the survey text I was using to decide where to go.
Suggested fix
Two things: (a) drop `text-transform:uppercase` from `#vistabox .vh` (or apply it only to the 'Planetfall —' prefix) so the lowercase region label actually reads as subordinate; (b) make the survey card and the journal draw the type label from the same field — right now the card shows the world archetype and the journal/vista show the landing biome under the same visual weight, so give them different words ('Cratered world' vs 'carbon flats') or show both on the card.
Reported by
cautious-newbie on surface-pro
Evidence
ipad-mini__06-survey-card: 'Mercury / CRATERED WORLD', biome line 'a face that remembers every impact'. ipad-mini__07-planetside header: 'PLANETFALL — MERCURY · CARBON WORLD'. ipad-mini__11-records Expedition Journal: 'Mercury Carbon world · 7/26'. These are two different entries in the same biome table (index.html:12773 `{k:'cratered', n:'Cratered world', f:'a face that remembers every impact'}` and 12777 `{k:'carbon', n:'Carbon world'}`). The developer knew (comment at index.html:12603 names this exact contradiction) and the attempted fix at 12608 lowercases the region so it reads 'visibly subordinate' — but `#vistabox .vh` carries `text-transform:uppercase` as an unscoped global rule (index.html:1651), so it renders in full caps exactly as loud as the card's label. The fix is defeated by its own stylesheet.
Impact
I chart worlds by what they are. If the card, the landing header and my own journal disagree about what I just stood on, my notes are worthless and I stop trusting the survey.
Suggested fix
Either exempt the region from the uppercase rule (`#vistabox .vh .region{text-transform:none;opacity:.75;font-weight:400}` and wrap the region in that span), or better, show both explicitly on the card too — 'Cratered world · landed in: carbon plains' — so the player learns that a world has many faces instead of reading it as a contradiction. The Records journal line should match whichever wording the card uses.
Reported by

major Small text still below WCAG AA contrastaccessibility 5 testers · 5 devices
Evidence
Sampled directly from 11-records.png (dpr 1, so these are CSS pixels), peak glyph colour against the panel background: Exotic 3.47:1, Primordial 3.56:1, Mythic 3.95:1, Rare 4.16:1; at the 98th percentile of stroke coverage they fall to 3.16, 3.34, 3.61 and 3.79:1. My sampling is calibrated — it read #ffcf8a and #b2bad8 back exactly on known text in the same shots. Source: #records .tier is font-size:8.5px (index.html:1445) and takes its colour from each tier's own hex (index.html:23901, RARITY_V17 at :3864). At 8.5px the strokes are so thin that antialiasing never lets them reach the nominal colour — measured Rare peaks at (51,115,213) against a nominal #3D8BFF of (61,139,255).
Impact
This is the panel the last round already flagged. It has come up off the floor but has not cleared AA, and the deeper problem is untouched: 8.5px is roughly half the size at which any contrast ratio is trustworthy. Ten labels I have to lean into the screen to read, on the board that is supposed to show off my progress.
Suggested fix
Raise #records .tier to at least 11px and lighten the four failing hexes toward their tints (Exotic #B98CFF, Primordial #F0836A, Mythic #F0709F, Rare #6FA8FF) — that puts all ten over 4.5:1 at a size where the stroke actually reaches its colour.
Reported by
accessibility on desktop-1080
Evidence
Measured off 13-prime-codex.png on the two grey sub-lines under every titan. 'relic blueprint on the claim' reads peak 4.25:1 (p98 3.98:1); the reach line '🏴 the basic elements lie near home — Earth among the first' reads peak 4.36:1 (p98 4.04:1). Both are 10.5px normal-weight (.psig .psub2, index.html:1109), so the AA bar is 4.5:1, not 3:1. The mechanism is visible in source: .psig.locked{opacity:0.85} (index.html:1097) multiplies --faint #828cb6 (index.html:22269) down to an effective (112,121,158). The developer's own comment at :1095 records the previous value as 0.62 and the resulting ratio as ~2.9:1 — so the change from 0.62 to 0.85 is real and measurable, it just stopped one step early.
Impact
The lore fix landed beautifully — all nine titans now have distinct, readable prose, which is the round's best content win. But the two guidance lines under each one, the lines that actually tell me where to go hunt, are the dimmest text in the panel. On the game's own goal screen, the instructions are the hardest part to read.
Suggested fix
Either raise .psig.locked opacity to 1.0 and dim only the .pic and .pchk, or change the inline color:var(--faint) at index.html:22269 to var(--dim). Either alone clears 4.5:1.
Reported by

major The control-hint pill truncates, hiding a core gesturereadability 5 testers · 5 devices
Evidence
Visible in iphone-se__02, 03, 04, 05 and 06: the hint pill reads 'Tap a planet to survey it · press Land on its card · dou…'. Source: the full string is 'Tap a planet to survey it · press Land on its card · double-tap zooms' (index.html:2269), and #hint sets white-space:nowrap; max-width:94vw; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis (index.html:850-853). At 375px it can never fit, so the ellipsis is permanent on this device.
Impact
This strip is the game's only always-on instruction, and it visibly promises a third thing I am not allowed to read. I do not enjoy working systems out by myself — I read the hint, saw it was cut, and simply never learned that double-tap zooms.
Suggested fix
Allow the hint to wrap to two lines on ≤420px (white-space:normal, text-align:center), or rotate the three tips one at a time on a timer. Never ellipsis the only instruction on screen.

The full string is at index.html:2269: '...· double-tap zooms'. The clipping is caused by index.html:850-853, which sets the hint to white-space:nowrap; max-width:94vw; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis — at 440px the third clause never fits.

Double-tap-to-zoom is the only way to read a world closely, and it is the one instruction the game never manages to finish saying. On a 440px phone this is not an edge case — it is the permanent state of the hint bar for the entire session, on ten of my twelve in-game screenshots.

Remove white-space:nowrap and let the pill wrap to two lines under 520px, or split the hint into a rotating single clause. If it must stay one line, shorten to 'Tap to survey · Land on the card · double-tap to zoom' — which fits.

major The survey card is excluded from the panel model — the dock overprints itlayout 4 testers · 4 devices
Evidence
pixel-7__06-survey-card.png: the card runs off the bottom of the viewport. 'ENVIRONMENT — Scorching; any surface water has boiled away. Low gravity' is tangled with the Charters/Compendium/Prime Codex/Shipyard chips, and 'PROCEDURAL SURVEY' is broken into 'PROCEDURAL ... VEY' by the trophy and bell circles. Same collision in 07, 08, 09, 11, 12, 14, 16 wherever the card is open underneath. Source: the BATCH B mobile block gives #setpanel, #tray, #chpanel, #codex, #log and #records 'bottom:calc(142px + safe-area)' plus a max-height (index.html:1720-1725) — #panel is not in that list and has no max-height anywhere; its only mobile rule is a width (index.html:1493). Its JS clamp is ay=clamp(..., _topMin, H-ph-12) (index.html:13674), which is viewport-aware but not dock-aware.
Impact
This is worse than unreadable — #recbtn, #bellwrap, #helpbtn and #setbtn are z-index:14 (index.html:167, 266, 1229, 1687) against the card's z-index:9, so taps aimed at the bottom of the card land on Records, Notifications, Guide or Settings instead. major The mouse system-mode hint omits scroll-to-zoom, so the only always-on legend never shows an exit from the starting systemdiscoverability 1 tester · 1 device
Evidence
ultrawide__05-system-map.png bottom pill reads exactly 'Hover a planet to preview · click to survey · press Land on its card' — three verbs, all of which keep you inside Sol. Source index.html:2271-2277, the non-touch HINTS map: `universe` says 'scroll to zoom in', `galaxy` says 'scroll toward one', `surface` says 'Scroll out to leave this world' — but `system` is the one string with no zoom verb at all. The touch variant of the same string DOES mention it ('double-tap zooms'). So the mouse hint is the single mode-string in the set that hides the wheel, and it is the mode a new player sits in for their whole first session.
Impact
I am the player who hates being funnelled. On my screen the visible affordances are eight planets and four corner boards; the persistent legend confirms I may hover, click and land. Nothing on screen suggests the sky above Sol is reachable. Field Training may cover it and the Guide's 'Getting Around' topic certainly does, but the hint pill is the game's always-visible teacher and here it contradicts its own three siblings.
Suggested fix
One-line change at index.html:2276 — make the non-touch system hint `Hover a planet to preview · click to survey · press Land on its card · scroll out for the galaxy`. If the pill is too long at narrow widths, drop the 'Hover a planet to preview' clause, which duplicates what the cursor already teaches.
Reported by
explorer on ultrawide
major The phrase 'your first charter' means two different things within forty secondsconsistency 1 tester · 1 device
Evidence
03-field-training: 'Welcome to Sol, Auditor — humanity's cradle and your first charter' (index.html:22913) — here a charter is a PLACE. 16-notifications, timestamped 41s later in the same session: 'Your charter board is open (Charters) — your first charter is accepted: Make planetfall' (index.html:23352) — here the identical three-word phrase is a QUEST. The same log also carries 'Sol is your charter for now' (index.html:23357) and 'The chapter rides atop your Charters board'. 12-charters shows a fourth register, '1 charter honored'. Source adds a fifth: index.html:22167 comments 'your charter grows as you claim Prime Codex signatures' (the reachable radius) and index.html:22191 fires a toast titled 'Beyond Your Charter' for flying too far.
Impact
A charter is simultaneously a star system, a reach radius, a quest board, a single quest, and a toast title. The word has been asked to carry the whole game and now carries nothing. When a player reads 'Sol is your charter for now' they cannot tell whether they have been assigned a territory or handed a to-do item, and 'Chapter' sitting one line away from 'Charters' makes it worse.
Suggested fix
Pick one meaning and rename the rest. Keep Charters = the quests (the board, the panel, 'Charter Complete', '1 charter honored'). Replace the place/reach sense everywhere: 'Sol is your charter for now' becomes 'Sol is your whole reach for now'; index.html:22913 becomes 'humanity's cradle and your first posting'; the index.html:22191 toast becomes 'Beyond Your Reach'. Then rename 'Chapter' to 'Expedition' so two near-homophones stop sharing a panel.

What the fleet caught that no tester could

A thousand sessions poke at states a storyboard never reaches. Two findings came only from the fleet, and both are regressions against a v1.7.0 baseline that was completely clean.

regressioncritical Null dereference crashes the survey card when the view leaves a star system 3 hits · 2 devices · 2 personas
Error
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'x') at describePick (index.html:5096) via renderPanel.
Cause
Line 5096 is the planet branch: star:{x:st.star.x, y:st.star.y, seed:st.star.seed}. There is no guard on st.star anywhere in describePick. When the camera leaves a system while a survey panel is still rendering, st.star is null and the render throws.
Who hit it
speedrunner and skimmer on laptop-768 and laptop-720 — the two fastest, most zoom-heavy personas. Both zoom out aggressively with a card open, which is exactly the sequence that triggers it.
Why it matters
v1.7.0 threw zero uncaught errors across 1,000 sessions. v1.7.3 throws this one. It is a frame-loop error, so it repeats every frame while the condition holds.
Suggested fix
Guard the star reference once at the top of describePick and fall back to the saved view: const S = st.star || (_savedView && _savedView.star) || null; then build where.star only when S is non-null.
regressionmajor The panel-model fix made the survey-card collision worse, not better measured across 21 profiles
Measurement
Overlapping-interactive-control defects went 85 → 243 across the 21-device sweep. Every one of the top offenders is a panel sitting on the survey card: Star Atlas row ∩ Land (8 devices), Guide topic ∩ + Add to Star Atlas (8), 📌 ∩ Planetside (8), ⛏ Mine Deposits ∩ ⇪ Save postcard (6).
Cause
The panel model gave every board a min-height floor, a title and more width — so the boards are now much bigger. But #panel (the survey card) appears in neither the PANELS registry that closePanels() walks, nor MODAL_SEL. It stays open underneath, and the bigger boards now cover far more of it than the small ones did.
Why it matters
The fix is sound; the omission inverts its benefit. Four testers independently described taps landing on the wrong layer. It is the clearest case in this round of a good change needing one more line.
Suggested fix
Add {id:'panel', el:()=>panelEl, open:()=>panelOpen, close:()=>hidePanel()} to PANELS so opening any board dismisses the card, and add #panel to MODAL_SEL so clicking the card doesn't close every board.

Performance — and a correction

I got this wrong twice, and the correction favours the game. My v1.7.0 report showed frame rate falling from 60fps to 45fps as backing-store size grew, and called it a real trend. It was not. Serving both builds side by side and alternating measurements under identical host state — the only way a frame-rate comparison between two builds means anything — puts every device at 60fps on both. The earlier curve was noise on this 2-core VM. There was never a performance problem to fix.

What I'd do next

The round worked. Twelve of fourteen findings are verifiably fixed, every persona scored higher, and the floor came up a full point. Mean 4.92 → 5.71 puts the build roughly where the roadmap predicted for Phase 0 plus part of Phase 1.
  1. Un-scope the panel model. The titled sheets, the min-height floor, the scrim and the top toast lane all live inside @media (max-width:900px), and the 1600px block is five width declarations. Everything from 901–1599px — Surface Pro, iPad Pro 13", iPad landscape, and every laptop — gets none of it. This is one media-query boundary standing between the work you already did and six more device profiles.
  2. Fix the five regressions. Three of them partly undo the fix that introduced them; the text-transform:uppercase one means a defect you deliberately fixed still renders unchanged.
  3. Then Phase 3 — accessibility. It is now the single largest gap in the panel: 2.5 against a mean of 5.71. The chrome improved a lot this round; the board and focus management are what remain.
